Subject: Internal: CareBridge RFI — technical notes draft

Kimberly / team — draft technical responses below. Please review and flag anything that needs Legal/Compliance language. I'm keeping the language operational and implementation-focused (procurement prefers this).

--- Draft snippet: Cross-border routing and lawful basis 
Redwood routes inference requests by policy (region, cost tier, and customer binding). For EU-origin requests you can choose: 
- EU-only processing (restrict routing to EU-hosted workers + KV cache stored in-region); or
- EU-first with fallback (prefer EU-hosted runtime; if capacity is unavailable, requests route to the nearest compatible region per your policy; these fallbacks are logged and visible in the Console).

Lawful basis: For controller customers, we process under your instruction as processor; we document transfers in the DPA annex and rely on standard contractual clauses / EU adequacy + DPF mappings where applicable. We include audit evidence of routing decisions (request trace + route justification) for the retention period in the SLA.

--- Draft snippet: KMS/HSM and keys
- Customer-managed keys (CMK) supported via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). HSM-backed keys supported where cloud providers offer them; Redwood's Private deployment supports direct HSM integration for on-prem and VPC configurations. 
- Scope: CMKs can be applied to long-term logs, artifacts, and backup storage. At present we do not encrypt ephemeral in-memory KV caches with CMK by default; we provide an opt-in path to persist encrypted KV snapshots to customer-owned storage for further encryption with CMK.

--- Draft snippet: Subprocessor & transfer matrix
Attached: transfer-matrix-carebridge.xlsx (workbook shows subprocessors, region, purpose, and data categories). We propose to inline the current 3rd-party vendor list in the DPA annex as Appendix B and provide monthly updates on changes.

Notes: Marcus, can you add a short paragraph about dedicated capacity (how it isolates tenant networking and disk) and the control-plane separation for Private deployments?

Thanks,
Ben
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-03T11:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: CareBridge RFI — technical notes draft

Adding the Dedicated/Private bulleted paragraph (for insertion into the playbook):

- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU pools provide compute isolation (tenant-only VMs/containers, encrypted disk, and isolated network overlays). Customers on Dedicated may request network peering or private endpoints; logs and object storage for model artifacts can be configured to persist in a customer-owned bucket.
- Private deployment: Offers complete control-plane partitioning. The customer's control plane runs in their VPC or on-prem, with optional air-gapped deployments. In this mode, Redwood operators do not have remote access to runtime instances; access is via customer-managed bastion or approved support channel under explicit access windows and logged for audit.

Also: we support route-level SLOs and automatic fallback policies that include model-variant substitution (smaller quantized model on fallback) to prevent complete failure when cross-border restrictions cause capacity constraints. This reduces data egress by favoring in-region caches and minimizes token-level retransmit.

Marcus
Senior Product Engineer — Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: CareBridge RFI: cross-border controls, DPA annex, and operational playbook

Emma — attaching the requested materials (see attachments list). Highlights: 

- Operational playbook (attached PDF): step-by-step flow for EU-origin processing, routing decisions, audit evidence capture, and fallback rules. Includes diagrams showing KV cache scoping and log flows.
- DPA annex draft (redwood-dpa-annex-draft-v1.docx): includes an inline subprocessor table and the proposed transfer mapping approach (we reference SCCs and DPF where relevant).
- Transfer matrix (attached spreadsheet): current list of subprocessors and regional mappings.

Short answers to your clarifying points: 
1) We support both "EU-only processing" (no fallback to non-EU) and "EU-first with fallback". The choice is customer-configurable per route and can be applied globally for an account or at the model/endpoint level.
2) We support HSM-backed customer-managed keys for logs, artifact storage, and backups. For ephemeral in-memory caches, our recommended pattern is: persist encrypted cache snapshots to customer-controlled storage using CMK/HSM if full in-region encryption is required. We will document recommended retention/rotation practices in the annex.

Next steps: 
- If LegalOps wants redline language, we'll accept edits to the attached docx and aim for a signature-ready annex within two weeks after agreement on subprocessors.
- Procurement: Ben and Jordan are available Friday for a 30-minute call to confirm isolation and SLA language. Please let me know availability and whether you'd like a short demo of routing logs in the Console.

Thanks — and happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the playbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference
